prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a narrow-room layout: nearby doorframes and walls form bright boundaries on the left and right, while the floor and central room recede into darker regions. The central standing person is roughly 1.5–2.5 m in front of the camera wearer, and the partly visible person on the ladder/right side is about 1–2 m away and approximately 1 m to the standing person’s right; the camera wearer’s raised hand/tool appears within about 0.3–0.7 m in frames 1 and 3. Across the five frames, the central person remains ahead but shifts from left-of-centre to right-of-centre as the camera turns, while nearby walls and the ladder sweep laterally; neither person shows a clear large approach or retreat. Depth makes near wall edges, foreground limbs, and clearance through the doorway easier to distinguish than RGB, but distances are only approximate because people merge with dark background regions, bright walls appear saturated, and thin tools or ladder parts have weak or missing depth boundaries.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map separates several person instances from the black background, showing one main person about 1.5–2.5 m ahead and another person partly cut off above/right near the ladder, with the two generally around 1–2 m apart. It also isolates the camera wearer’s foreground arm or held object near the lower/central edge, placing it within arm’s reach, while the standing people and most floor objects remain beyond the wearer’s reach; small elongated masks near their hands suggest nearby handheld objects. Across the frames, the principal person mask moves from left-of-centre through centre to right-of-centre, while partial people enter or leave the top and side borders as the camera rotates; overlapping masks expose occlusion between bodies, hands, and foreground objects. This map reveals instance boundaries that are difficult to follow in the cluttered RGB, but it is unreliable in class identity and completeness: the tool, broom, ladder, limbs, and foreground arm are variously labelled as suitcase, skateboard, handbag, cellphone, or person, and much of the room structure is omitted.
descriptions.pose: The pose map gives the clearest body geometry for the main standing person, who remains roughly 1.5–2.5 m ahead, upright, and mostly facing the camera wearer, with the head oriented generally toward the camera although exact gaze cannot be established. Shoulder, torso, arm, and leg joints show the person shifting from left-of-centre to centre and then right-of-centre as viewpoint changes, with modest apparent turning but no strong approach or retreat; their hands lie near waist-to-chest height, while the camera wearer’s detected magenta hands in frame 4 are much nearer and within arm’s reach. The second person near the ladder is largely absent because only cropped lower-body regions are visible, and limbs or hands outside the image boundaries or behind objects are not reconstructed. Pose makes facing direction, joint height, limb extension, and hand proximity clearer than RGB, but it is unreliable where head points scatter, limbs are truncated or asymmetrical, magenta hand detections appear only intermittently, and nearby objects receive no spatial representation.
